editorial:
Imagine being a pro at fixing other people's minds while your own love life is a total wreck. That is exactly where you find the main character in this quirky 1960s gem. She is a smart psychotherapist who knows all the tricks in the book, but when it comes to her own heart, she is a nervous mess. The movie feels like a lighthearted dance between professional logic and messy human emotions. You will find yourself rooting for her as she tries to navigate her own fears while accidentally getting tangled up in the romantic dramas of her own patients. It is a funny look at how we often give the best advice to others but cannot follow it ourselves.

What really makes this work is the great acting and the way the story keeps you guessing. The pacing is steady and the comedic timing is spot on for the era. While some of the plot twists feel a bit old-fashioned, the charm of the characters carries it through. If you enjoy old-school romantic comedies with a bit of a psychological twist, you should definitely give this one a try. You can easily find it for rent on Apple TV or stream it in high definition on Prime Video for a cozy movie night. Adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is also a great move if you love vintage cinema.
endingExplained: By the end, the therapist finally stops hiding behind her medical books and faces her own fears. After causing a bit of chaos in her patients' lives, she realizes that she cannot heal others if she is broken inside. She lets go of her neuroses and opens her heart to a real relationship. The movie wraps up with her finding a healthy balance between her career and her personal happiness, proving that love is the best medicine.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic rom-coms and stories about personal growth.
